newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia PM talks fruitless, compromise sought.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia PM talks fruitless, compromise sought.

text.p: Slovenian President Milan Kucan said on Thursday two rounds of talks with political parties had failed to bring an agreement on who should head the next government.

Kucan told a news conference he hoped fresh negotiations also involving Constitutional Court president Anton Jerovsek, central bank governor France Arhar and State Council president Ivan Kristan would end the stalemate.
"Maybe they can help me search for a way out of this situation," Kucan said, adding that he aimed to name a prime minister by the end of the year.
Inconclusive parliamentary elections on November 10 have made Kucan's task difficult and on Thursday he said the parties remained entrenched in their positions.
"For now the parties are not ready to rethink their positions and start looking for new coalition possibilities," he said.
Support was divided between incumbent Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek of the centre-left Liberal Democrats and Marjan Podobnik, who heads the conservative People's Party, he explained.
The Liberal Democrats won the most votes in Slovenia's November 10 general election, gaining 25 seats in the 90-seat parliament.
The People's Party is the biggest of the three rightist parties that have formed the so-called "Spring" alliance. Together they hold 45 seats, just one short of an absolute majority.
"The parties are starting to realise that a firm insistence on their current positions will bring no result," Kucan said.
Under the constitution he must decide on a prime minister by January 3.
